question.text: In a Category III AIF desk structure, the Operations Manager typically oversees which combination of functions?

answer.text: Trade execution support, post-trade reconciliation with custodian/PB, NAV checks, and investor subscription/redemption workflows.
Drafting of Private Placement Memorandum and merchant-banker liaison.
Final investment decisions for all portfolio positions.

explanation.text: The Logic: The Operations Manager in a Cat III AIF handles the non-investment operational spine: coordinating trade settlements with custodian and PB, post-trade reconciliations, NAV review against fund-administrator output, stamp-duty tracking with RTA, investor subscription and redemption workflow, and regulatory reporting deadlines. Deal sourcing and investment decisions sit with the CIO; PPM drafting sits with legal + merchant banker. The Trap: Options A and D conflate operations with investment function. Option C places PPM drafting outside its legal-function home. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XIX-D test operations-manager scope similarly. XXI-B has an analogous role for PM operations. Manager's Pro-Tip: The Operations Manager is your first line of defence against reconciliation breaks — daily PB margin call vs custodian demat vs FA NAV. Set a three-way daily recon protocol with T+1 hard deadline. Any break > 1 bp of NAV escalates to CIO. This catches everything from trade-booking errors to corporate-action miscreates.
